question: From 30 December 2024, all operators and traders placing relevant products on the EU market will be required, under the Deforestation Regulation1, to prove that their products have been deforestationfree since 31 December 2020.

However, many technical questions about the practicalities of implementation remain unanswered, the new EU information system for uploading due diligence statements is still in the early stages of development, many Member States missed the deadline to designate their competent authorities, and primary forests have not been mapped across the EU.

A growing number of voices, both within and outside the EU, are now warning that this lack of clarity prevents large companies from adequately preparing for compliance and could lead to widespread disruptions in European and global supply chains. 1.

Given the persistent lack of clarity regarding the interpretation and application of the rules, does the Commission plan to grant an additional grace period to operators and traders to give them enough time to adapt to the new rules?

Will the new EU information system allow the automatic transfer of data from operators and traders, as opposed to manual data entry, which would generate an unmanageable administrative burden and a risk of human error?

Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 (OJ L 150, 9.6.2023, p. 206).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.4.2024) The Commission engaged in different streams of work to raise clarity about the interpretation and application of the provisions of the Deforestation Regulation1.

To facilitate the stakeholders’ preparation the Commission has published on its website the second version of Frequently Asked Questions2, which now consists of more than 80 answers and covers clarifications on traceability and due diligence obligations, definitions, the Information System, information on relevant programmes and partnerships, and dialogue with third countries, among many other topics.

A new update is currently under drafting which will address more than 20 additional questions based on the inputs received from stakeholders. The Commission is also working on a Guidance document on the implementation of the Regulation, which will provide interpretation for different areas and tangible examples for implementation.

The development of the Information System reached the phase that allowed pilot testing of the existing features with more than 100 private stakeholders. The Commission is currently analysing the feedbacks to ensure that the production version will be a fully functional system with relevant functionalities in place.

An Application Programming Interface is also under development to allow machine-tomachine connection between stakeholders’ systems and the Information System, which shall be deployed in the Information System by the entry into application.

According to Article 38, the Regulation will enter into full application for large and middle enterprises from 30 December 2024, while for small and micro-undertakings the entry into application is from 30 June 2025.
1 Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making

available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 (OJ L 150, 9.6.2023, p. 206). 2 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/frequently-asked-questions-deforestation-regulation_en
